requirement_paraphrase: Run a security programme for the automation and control systems, with its own scope, owner and objectives
building_ot_example: BMS, lighting control, AV, CCTV and access control sit with Facilities, not IT, and are left out of the ISMS
gap_or_note: ISO can cover building OT only if the ISMS scope names it. In practice the scope stops at the corporate network
evidence_to_ask_for: ISMS scope statement that names building systems; named owner for each system; programme plan

requirement_paraphrase: Keep a current inventory of control system components, including firmware and network location
building_ot_example: DDC controllers, IP cameras, lift gateways, AV matrices and DSPs, plant-room routers
gap_or_note: A.5.9 already asks for all associated assets. The weak point is discovery: building devices rarely appear in IT tools, so the list is built by walking the site
evidence_to_ask_for: Inventory with firmware version, IP or VLAN, owner and maintaining contractor; date of last site walk

requirement_paraphrase: Assess risk per zone, including health, safety, environmental and physical consequences, not just data loss
building_ot_example: Smoke control, lift recall, chilled water for a server room, access control on fire exits
gap_or_note: ISO risk is framed on confidentiality, integrity and availability of information. 62443 adds safety and physical outcomes and assesses each zone
evidence_to_ask_for: Zone-level risk assessment that scores life-safety and operational impact

requirement_paraphrase: Partition the system into zones and conduits and document the model
building_ot_example: BMS, CCTV, AV and guest Wi-Fi as separate zones; the integrator's cloud link to the BMS as a conduit
gap_or_note: ISO asks for network segregation but not a documented zone and conduit model
evidence_to_ask_for: Zone and conduit diagram; list of conduits with owner and permitted traffic

requirement_paraphrase: Set a target security level (SL-T 1 to 4) for each zone and justify it
building_ot_example: A hotel BMS zone at SL-T 2; a hospital smoke-control zone at SL-T 3
gap_or_note: No ISO equivalent. Security levels are what turn a zone model into buildable requirements
evidence_to_ask_for: Zone register with SL-T and rationale; sign-off by asset owner

requirement_paraphrase: Require integrators and maintainers to show defined security capabilities: remote access, patching, backup, staff competence, incident handling
building_ot_example: BMS integrator with permanent remote support; AV integrator who keeps the only copy of the control code
gap_or_note: ISO asks for security in supplier agreements. 62443-2-4 lists what the service provider must actually be able to do. Note: IE is a service provider under this part
evidence_to_ask_for: Integrator capability statement against 2-4; contract clauses; last review of integrator access

requirement_paraphrase: Patch control systems through a managed process: vendor-qualified patches, testing, planned windows, compensating controls when a patch is not possible
building_ot_example: Head-end PC on an old Windows build because the BMS vendor has not qualified newer versions
gap_or_note: ISO expects timely patching. OT often cannot patch on IT timescales, so the gap is the documented exception and the compensating control
evidence_to_ask_for: Patch status per component; vendor qualification records; exception register with compensating controls

requirement_paraphrase: Identify and authenticate every human user on every interface
building_ot_example: Shared 'admin' login on the BMS front end and the AV touch panel
gap_or_note: Requirement matches. Many building devices cannot support individual accounts, so expect exceptions
evidence_to_ask_for: User list per system; evidence that shared accounts are removed or controlled

requirement_paraphrase: Identify and authenticate software processes and devices (SL 2 and above)
building_ot_example: Controllers accept BACnet or Modbus commands from any device on the network
gap_or_note: ISO secure authentication is written mainly for users. Legacy building protocols have no device authentication, so segmentation carries the load
evidence_to_ask_for: Protocol inventory; secure protocol options in use (for example BACnet Secure Connect); compensating segmentation

requirement_paraphrase: Manage accounts: create, change, disable and remove
building_ot_example: Integrator engineer accounts left active after handover
evidence_to_ask_for: Joiner, mover and leaver records for OT accounts; quarterly access review

requirement_paraphrase: Manage authenticators, including changing defaults
building_ot_example: Default passwords on IP cameras and DDC controllers
gap_or_note: Default credentials are the most common finding on a building site walk
evidence_to_ask_for: Evidence defaults changed at commissioning; credential vault entries

requirement_paraphrase: Enforce password strength where passwords are used
building_ot_example: Four-digit PIN on a lighting control panel
evidence_to_ask_for: Password policy applied to OT systems or recorded exception

requirement_paraphrase: Monitor and control all access from untrusted networks, including remote access
building_ot_example: Vendor remote tool on the BMS head end; 4G router in the plant room; cloud-connected lift monitoring
gap_or_note: ISO covers remote working. 62443 requires every untrusted-network path to be known, approved and monitored, which is where hidden connections are found
evidence_to_ask_for: Remote access register; session logs; approval records; result of a hidden-connection walk

requirement_paraphrase: Enforce authorisation, least privilege and separation of duties
building_ot_example: Every operator can change setpoints and alarm limits
evidence_to_ask_for: Role matrix for each OT system

requirement_paraphrase: Control portable and mobile devices that connect to the control system
building_ot_example: Engineer laptop plugged into a controller during maintenance
evidence_to_ask_for: Portable device rule for contractors; scan or approval record before connection

requirement_paraphrase: Generate audit records for security-relevant events
building_ot_example: BMS head end logs alarms but not who changed a setpoint
gap_or_note: Requirement matches; the device often cannot log. Record the limitation
evidence_to_ask_for: Sample logs showing user, action and time

requirement_paraphrase: Timestamp audit records from a synchronised source
building_ot_example: Controllers with drifting clocks make incident timelines unreliable
evidence_to_ask_for: NTP configuration for OT components

requirement_paraphrase: Protect the integrity of information in transit
building_ot_example: Unencrypted BACnet/IP and Modbus TCP between controllers
gap_or_note: Legacy protocols cannot meet this natively. Rate it a compensated gap, not a pass
evidence_to_ask_for: Protocol list; compensating segmentation; secure protocol roadmap

requirement_paraphrase: Protect against malicious code
building_ot_example: Head-end PC with no anti-malware because the vendor will not support it
gap_or_note: Use vendor-approved anti-malware or application allow-listing
evidence_to_ask_for: Anti-malware or allow-listing status per OT host; vendor approval

requirement_paraphrase: Verify that security functions work, including at factory and site acceptance
building_ot_example: Site acceptance test checks the HVAC sequences but no security settings
gap_or_note: ISO A.8.29 is aimed at development and acceptance of systems. 62443 expects security checks in FAT and SAT and during operation
evidence_to_ask_for: FAT and SAT scripts with security test cases; results

requirement_paraphrase: Detect unauthorised changes to software and firmware
building_ot_example: Controller firmware updated by a subcontractor without record
gap_or_note: ISO controls installation and change. 62443 adds integrity checking of the software itself
evidence_to_ask_for: Firmware baseline and hash or version check; change records

requirement_paraphrase: Protect confidentiality of information at rest and in transit where required
building_ot_example: Floor plans and access-control databases on the BMS server
evidence_to_ask_for: Classification applied to OT data; encryption where supported

requirement_paraphrase: Segment control system networks from other networks
building_ot_example: BMS on the same flat network as guest Wi-Fi
evidence_to_ask_for: Network diagram; VLAN and firewall evidence

requirement_paraphrase: Protect zone boundaries: deny by default, allow by exception
building_ot_example: Any-to-any rule between the corporate LAN and the BMS VLAN
evidence_to_ask_for: Firewall rule review for each conduit

requirement_paraphrase: Make audit logs accessible and monitor the control system continuously
building_ot_example: A SIEM fed only by Microsoft 365 and endpoints sees nothing from the BMS
gap_or_note: ISO lets the organisation set monitoring scope. 62443 expects the control system itself to be monitored, which usually needs passive OT network monitoring
evidence_to_ask_for: Log sources list including OT; monitoring coverage map; alert samples

requirement_paraphrase: Keep essential functions running under denial-of-service conditions
building_ot_example: Network storm takes down the BMS and the cooling for a data room
gap_or_note: ISO covers capacity and redundancy, not degraded-mode operation of essential functions
evidence_to_ask_for: Degraded-mode design notes; test results

requirement_paraphrase: Back up the control system and be able to recover and rebuild it
building_ot_example: Controller programs held only by the integrator
gap_or_note: ISO backup applies. The common gap is ownership: the client holds no copy of its own control code
evidence_to_ask_for: Client-held backups of programs and configs; last restore test

requirement_paraphrase: Document and control network and security configuration settings
building_ot_example: Switch and firewall configs for the BMS network not under change control
evidence_to_ask_for: Configuration baseline; change records

requirement_paraphrase: Run only the functions, ports and services that are needed
building_ot_example: Web server, Telnet and FTP left enabled on controllers
evidence_to_ask_for: Hardening checklist results per device type

requirement_paraphrase: Security measures must not stop essential functions such as safety and life-safety systems
building_ot_example: Account lockout or MFA on an operator station that blocks smoke-control override in an emergency
gap_or_note: No ISO equivalent. A control that is correct for IT can be dangerous in a building
evidence_to_ask_for: Essential functions register; test showing security controls do not block emergency operation

requirement_paraphrase: Specify secure products and secure vendor development when buying control system components
building_ot_example: Tender for new access control says nothing about security capability
gap_or_note: ISO covers ICT supply chain security in general. 62443-4-1 and 4-2 give a recognised certification to ask for
evidence_to_ask_for: Procurement clauses; vendor 4-1 or component 4-2 certificates where available
